name: PromptZone
tagline: Free community for AI prompts, model news, and practitioner discussion

pricing.notes: Free to join, read, and post; no paid tier.

verdictSummary: The software is explicitly not the moat: PromptZone runs on Forem, the open-source platform behind dev.to, so you can self-host the entire codebase in an afternoon and get a working, empty forum. A personal prompt vault is a genuine one-sitting build and the prompt below produces one. What a solo build cannot generate is the members: the community prompt archive, feedback on what holds up per model, and the daily discussion are network value, not code.
coreLoopDIY: Build a single-user prompt vault: save, tag, search, version, and copy your own AI prompts.
requirements: optional $5 VPS if you want it online
whatYouLose: community-contributed prompts you did not have to write
feedback on which prompts hold up per model
discovery of new techniques as models change
an audience for the prompts you publish
daily curated AI news and discussion
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays: PromptZone is free, so the honest question is why people show up instead of DIY. A vault stores prompts you already wrote; a community surfaces prompts, failure reports, and model-specific tweaks from other practitioners, and an audience reads what you publish. That is the part no solo build produces.

notes: Owner-submitted; the software layer is open source (Forem), so the DIY prompt builds the personal vault, not the community.
prompt:
Build me a personal prompt vault to keep my AI prompts organized. Requirements:

- Scope honestly: single user, my prompts only. If I want other people's
  prompts and feedback on mine, that is a community (PromptZone, or
  self-hosted Forem), and no solo build replaces it; say so in the README.
- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered EJS plus htmx, no build
  step.
- Prompts have a title, body in Markdown (marked), tags, and a target model
  field (claude, gpt, gemini, other).
- Full-text search across title, body, and tags with SQLite FTS5; filter by
  tag and by target model.
- Every edit keeps the previous body as a version; show a version list per
  prompt with one-click restore.
- One-click copy-to-clipboard on every prompt, in list and detail views.
- Import and export the whole vault as a single JSON file.
- One shared password from .env in front of every route; no accounts.
- Runs locally with node server.js; also deploys on a $5 VPS behind Caddy;
  one SQLite file with a nightly dump.
- Out of scope: publishing, comments, voting, feeds, and profiles. The
  community is the part you cannot vibe-code.
- README: setup, password note, and backup instructions.
